# Ratings, spreads and credit-commentary ledger — hyperscalers and neoclouds (2024-01-01 to 2026-09-11)

Method. Every value below was read on the page or filing linked in the row. Coupons, yields and spreads come from the issuers' own SEC pricing term sheets (Form FWP) or 8-K/6-K press-release exhibits; agency actions come from S&P's public rating-action pages (read in the browser), Moody's public press-release page where one exists, and dated press coverage where the agency page is behind a login (flagged in `sourceType`). Nothing is estimated. Where a value could not be found it is listed under notFound.

## A. What the ledger shows

1. Oracle is the credit story. Its own term sheets print the migration: Baa2/BBB/BBB all stable (Sep 2024, Jan 2025) -> Baa2 negative / BBB negative / BBB stable (Sep 2025, Feb 2026) -> S&P downgrade to BBB-/A-3 stable on 9 Jul 2026. Its new-issue spread to Treasuries widened from +70/+138 bps (Sep 2024, 5y/40y) to +95/+195 bps (Feb 2026, 3y/40y) while the ICE BofA BBB index OAS was flat at 0.93-0.95 pct on those dates (FRED BAMLC0A4CBBB), so the widening is issuer-specific. S&P's 9 Jul 2026 note is the only agency page that prints a funding gap: FY2027 capex guidance $90-95bn, FOCF deficit "nearly $42 billion" FY2027 and "around $25 billion" FY2028, RPO $638bn, $260bn of additional lease commitments.
2. Amazon, Alphabet and Meta kept their ratings but Moody's took Amazon's positive outlook away (20 Feb 2026, capex ~$200bn) and S&P now forecasts two years of negative reported FOCF at Amazon and lower FOCF at Alphabet in 2026-27. Alphabet answered with an $84.75bn equity raise (2 Jun 2026: $18bn common, $16.75bn 6.25% mandatory convertible preferred, $40bn ATM, $10bn Berkshire private placement). New-issue spreads: Alphabet USD T+27/+95 (Feb 2026) -> T+33/+130 (Aug 2026); Amazon T+30/+130 (Mar 2026, incl. a 50-year) -> T+40/+125 (Jul 2026); Meta T+50/+110 (Oct 2025) -> T+53/+147 (Apr 2026).
3. Microsoft has issued no bonds since 2024 and keeps Aaa/AAA; Moody's Aug 2026 affirmation still cites $329bn of uncommenced lease obligations and a ~$4bn cumulative FCF deficit FY2027-28.
4. Neocloud price of capital, from their own filings: CoreWeave unsecured 9.000-9.750% (2025-26) and €8.500%; contract-backed DDTLs SOFR+225 (A3/A(low), Meta MSA) to SOFR+450/+550 (Ba2/BB+, non-IG customers); converts 1.75%. Applied Digital secured 9.250% at 97 (Nov 2025) -> 6.750% at 98 (Mar 2026, Oracle lease) -> 7.000% at par (Jun 2026). Cipher 7.125% -> 6.125% -> 6.000% secured (Google warrant pledge on the first). TeraWulf 7.750% and 7.250% secured (Fluidstack JVs, Google warrant pledge). IREN 5.96% fixed notes plus SOFR+225 DDTL on its Microsoft contract; converts 0.00-3.50%. Nebius converts 0.50-4.50% and a first asset-backed facility at SOFR+250.
5. Regulators now name the mechanism. Fed FSR (May 2026): cloud-computing IG bond issuance "neared $100 billion in the first quarter"; survey respondents flag that AI "capital expenditures are increasingly funded by debt". IMF GFSR (Apr 2026): "$3.4 trillion in AI-related capital expenditure through 2029"; hyperscalers "raised more than $100 billion in bond financing since January 2025"; Box 1.3 reproduces Morgan Stanley's Jul-2025 funding stack (capex ~$2.9tn through 2028 vs hyperscaler cash flow $1.4tn, private bilateral credit $0.8tn, other capital $0.35tn, corporate debt $0.2tn, ABS/CMBS $0.15tn). BIS Bulletin 120 (Jan 2026): private credit to AI-related firms "over $200 billion", "over $40 billion" originated in 2025, spreads 6.2 vs 6.1 pp for non-AI. FSB (May 2026): AI's share of private credit deals 34% in 2025 vs 17% average prior five years. BoE FSR (Jul 2026): consensus 2028 hyperscaler capex "now over $1 trillion" vs "less than $600 billion" in Dec 2025; the five hyperscalers were 3% of US IG stock but >15% of YTD issuance by early May; Barclays projects $240bn of 2026 needs via IG issuance.
